sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的队伍。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受nytimes.com/subscribe上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittrowev.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的娜塔莉·基特罗夫。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Across America, hundreds of towns and cities are trying to get guns off the streets by turning them over to businesses that offer to destroy them.
sentences.zh: 在美国各地，数百个城镇和城市正试图通过将枪支交给承诺销毁它们的商家，来清理街头的枪支。

sentences.en: But a New York Times investigation found that something very different is happening.
sentences.zh: 但《纽约时报》的一项调查发现，实际情况却大相径庭。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Mike McIntyre on the unintended consequences of efforts by local officials to rid their communities of guns.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事迈克·麦金泰尔将讲述地方官员为清理社区枪支所做努力带来的意外后果。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, January 9th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月9日，星期二。

sentences.en: Mike, you cover guns in America where gun possession is a uniquely protected right, which means that getting guns out of circulation is an uphill battle.
sentences.zh: 迈克，你负责报道美国的枪支问题，在这里，持枪是一项受到独特保护的权利，这意味着让枪支退出流通是一场艰苦的战斗。

sentences.en: And I understand you've been looking into that.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，你一直在调查这件事。

sentences.en: Tell me about your reporting.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说你的报道吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, we've been looking a lot at the issues of gun violence, gun culture, gun commerce in the United States because with more than 400 million firearms
sentences.zh: 是的，我们一直在深入研究美国的枪支暴力、枪支文化和枪支贸易问题，因为这里有超过4亿支枪支，

sentences.en: in the civilian population, it continues to be a major issue of public debate.
sentences.zh: 在平民手中，这依然是公众辩论的一个重大议题。

sentences.en: And a lot of that debate has centered around the easy accessibility of guns, how simple it is to be able to purchase one, the types of firepower involved,
sentences.zh: 很多辩论都集中在枪支获取的便利性上，比如购买一支枪有多简单，涉及的火力类型，

sentences.en: and the havoc that they can wreak.
sentences.zh: 以及它们可能造成的破坏。

sentences.en: I mean, gun violence actually surpassed car crashes recently in terms of the most common cause of deaths for children and adolescents.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，枪支暴力最近实际上已经超过了车祸，成为儿童和青少年最常见的死亡原因。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: More than half of the gun violence-related deaths are suicides.
sentences.zh: 超过一半的枪支暴力相关死亡是自杀。

sentences.en: So, there's every reason to be looking at the scourge of gun violence.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们有充分的理由去审视枪支暴力这一祸害。

sentences.en: But there's also this other side of it that doesn't get a lot of attention, which is, you know, what happens to guns that nobody wants anymore?
sentences.zh: 但这件事还有另一面，却没得到太多关注，那就是，那些没人想要的枪支最后都去哪了？

sentences.en: And so we started taking a look at what that process looks like and discovered that it's actually not quite as simple as you might think.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开始研究这个过程，结果发现它其实并不像你想象的那么简单。

sentences.en: Okay, just to back up a second, say more about what guns we're talking about here, these unwanted guns that are up for disposal.
sentences.zh: 好的，先退一步，详细说说我们在这里讨论的是哪些枪支，这些等待处理的闲置枪支。

sentences.en: So, police departments have a tendency to become almost like landfills or repositories for firearms that come into their possession through any number of ways.
sentences.zh: 警察局往往会变成枪支的“垃圾填埋场”或仓库，这些枪支通过各种途径进入他们手中。

sentences.en: Sometimes guns are confiscated from crime scenes.
sentences.zh: 有时是从犯罪现场没收的枪支。

sentences.en: You get people turning in guns that they don't want.
sentences.zh: 有时是人们主动上交他们不想要的枪支。

sentences.en: Other times, it's the police agencies themselves that are trying to upgrade their service weapons,
sentences.zh: 还有些时候，是警察机构自己想要升级他们的制式武器，

sentences.en: and so they wind up with an inventory of old ones that they need something to do with.
sentences.zh: 于是他们最终积压了一批旧武器，需要找地方处理。

sentences.en: And especially at larger police departments, you very quickly, as you might imagine, end up with storage lockers and evidence rooms just, you know, chock full of guns
sentences.zh: 特别是在大型警察局，你可以想象，很快就会出现储物柜和证物室里塞满了枪支，

sentences.en: and related equipment.
sentences.zh: 以及相关设备的情况。

sentences.en: This is obviously a liability problem.
sentences.zh: 这显然是一个责任问题。

sentences.en: I mean, you get situations where guns have disappeared from police departments.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，会出现枪支从警察局失踪的情况。

sentences.en: You get other cases in which guns are sold or auctioned off because they just need to free up space,
sentences.zh: 还有些案例中，枪支被出售或拍卖，因为他们需要腾出空间，

sentences.en: and then it winds up being reused again in a crime, sometimes even against police.
sentences.zh: 结果这些枪又被用于犯罪，有时甚至是对付警察。

sentences.en: So there's a whole lot of controversy about what happens to these guns, but that basically is why the police are in the situation of having to figure out how to dispose of them
sentences.zh: 所以关于这些枪支的去向存在很多争议，但基本上这就是为什么警察不得不设法处理它们，

sentences.en: because they just simply wind up with more than they know what to do with.
sentences.zh: 因为他们手里的枪实在多到不知道该怎么办了。

sentences.en: Okay, so basically these are guns that are just hanging around, and the police need to do something with them.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以基本上这些枪就是闲置在那里，警察需要处理掉它们。

sentences.en: And more and more, they're trying to destroy these guns and take them out of circulation.
sentences.zh: 而且他们越来越多地尝试销毁这些枪支，让它们退出流通。

sentences.en: Right, but there is a sort of interesting subset that has increased in recent years, and that is the population of guns that are turned into what they call buyback prograMs.
sentences.zh: 没错，但近年来出现了一个有趣的细分群体，那就是通过所谓的“枪支回购计划”上交的枪支。

sentences.en: And these are programs in which governments or sometimes nonprofit organizations like churches especially will offer incentives for people to turn in guns that they don't want,
sentences.zh: 这些计划是指政府或有时是非营利组织（尤其是教会）提供激励措施，让人们上交不想要的枪支，

sentences.en: either through cash payments or sometimes grocery store gift cards, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 通过现金支付或有时是超市礼品卡之类的方式。

sentences.en: There's not a lot of research that suggests that they do much to reduce crime, which has led to some criticism of these by gun rights advocates.
sentences.zh: 并没有太多研究表明这些计划在减少犯罪方面有多大作用，这导致了一些枪支权利倡导者的批评。

sentences.en: However, there's also sort of a logic to why they might want to be done in the sense that, if nothing else, they would remove guns from unstable situations,
sentences.zh: 然而，这种做法也有其逻辑，即至少它们能将枪支从不稳定的环境中移除，

sentences.en: households in which there's a concern that a gun being present might contribute to a tragic event, like a suicide or a domestic violence incident,
sentences.zh: 比如在担心枪支存在可能导致悲剧事件（如自杀或家庭暴力）的家庭中，

sentences.en: or a child getting a hold of it and hurting his or herself or someone else.
sentences.zh: 或者防止孩子拿到枪伤害自己或他人。

sentences.en: So buybacks have become increasingly popular, and they are making up more and more of the firearms that police wind up having to dispose of.
sentences.zh: 所以回购计划变得越来越受欢迎，它们在警察需要处理的枪支中所占比例也越来越大。

sentences.en: Okay, so Mike, how have they been destroying all these guns, both the police surplus ones and the guns from the buyback programs?
sentences.zh: 好的，迈克，他们一直是如何销毁这些枪支的，包括警察的剩余物资和回购计划中的枪支？

sentences.en: So traditionally, the way that guns are disposed of has been very limited means.
sentences.zh: 传统上，处理枪支的方法非常有限。

sentences.en: There's a surprisingly small number of approved methods that the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms,
sentences.zh: 美国酒精、烟草和火器管理局（ATF）批准的方法少得惊人，

sentences.en: which is the regulatory agency overseeing guns in the United States, says are acceptable.
sentences.zh: 该机构是美国监管枪支的机构。

sentences.en: And in the past, it really boiled down to one of two ways.
sentences.zh: 过去，基本上只有两种方法。

sentences.en: One was to put it through a smelter at a steel mill and literally melt it down.
sentences.zh: 一种是放入钢铁厂的熔炉里直接熔化。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Another was to use a blowtorch to make a series of cuts in the firearm to make sure that it's rendered inoperable and basically reduce it to three or four pieces.
sentences.zh: 另一种是用喷灯在枪支上切几刀，确保它无法使用，基本上将其分解成三四块。

sentences.en: And other methods that have been used in the past would be simply trying to smash it with a sledgehammer.
sentences.zh: 过去使用过的其他方法还包括直接用大锤砸碎。

sentences.en: That's all kind of medieval.
sentences.zh: 那听起来太原始了。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're right.
sentences.zh: 是的，你说得对。

sentences.en: I mean, the problem, as you might guess, is that, first of all, some of these are dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如你所料，问题首先在于其中一些方法很危险。

sentences.en: And secondly, they're not guaranteed to work completely.
sentences.zh: 其次，它们不能保证彻底销毁。

sentences.en: And then thirdly, they can be expensive.
sentences.zh: 第三，它们可能很昂贵。

sentences.en: If you're going to use a torch to do a whole lot of guns, you're probably going to have to pay a gunsmith or someone like that to do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你要用喷灯处理大量枪支，你可能得花钱请枪匠或类似的人来做。

sentences.en: So police departments literally take those guns to a smelter or someone who just smashes it to smithereens.
sentences.zh: 所以警察局干脆把那些枪送到熔炼厂，或者找人把它们砸得粉碎。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's traditionally the way it's been done in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这在过去一直是处理方式。

sentences.en: But about a decade ago, there was a new process introduced that began to change things a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但大约十年前，出现了一种新的工艺，开始改变现状。

sentences.en: Interestingly, it was introduced by a former police officer himself.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，它是由一位前警官本人引入的。

sentences.en: It was a fellow named Ray Reynolds from the St. Louis Police Department who had retired in the late 1980s and gone to work for a couple of gun companies.
sentences.zh: 那个人叫雷·雷诺兹，来自圣路易斯警察局，他在20世纪80年代末退休，后来为几家枪支公司工作。

sentences.en: And he then started his own business of helping police departments trade in their unwanted or old service weapons to use as credit to purchase new ones.
sentences.zh: 然后他创办了自己的公司，帮助警察局以旧换新，用不想要的或旧的制式武器作为购买新武器的抵扣额。

sentences.en: And somewhere along the line, he saw an opening in the whole area of how to dispose of guns.
sentences.zh: 在某个阶段，他看到了枪支处理领域的一个商机。

sentences.en: New at six, pulverizing pistols.
sentences.zh: 六点新闻报道：粉碎手枪。

sentences.en: A local company is helping collect and destroy unwanted guns.
sentences.zh: 一家本地公司正在帮助收集和销毁多余的枪支。

sentences.en: And Reynolds created this company called Gunbusters.
sentences.zh: 雷诺兹创建了这家名为“枪支终结者”（Gunbusters）的公司。

sentences.en: Tonight, an up-close look at this metal-mashing machine.
sentences.zh: 今晚，近距离观察这台金属粉碎机。

sentences.en: Which developed a machine called a firearms pulverizer.
sentences.zh: 他们开发了一种名为“枪支粉碎机”的机器。

sentences.en: He had it patented in 2014, and they put video cameras inside it.
sentences.zh: 他在2014年获得了专利，他们在机器内部安装了摄像机。

sentences.en: And so you could actually videotape the destruction process and see it happening.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以录下销毁过程，亲眼看到它发生。

sentences.en: And so his idea was to take this and use that machine to destroy the gun quickly and easily.
sentences.zh: 他的想法就是利用这台机器快速简便地销毁枪支。

sentences.en: This was his innovation, that it was a way for police departments to avoid having to deal with steel mills, avoid having to deal with blowtorches and sledgehammers,
sentences.zh: 这就是他的创新之处，让警察局不必再与钢铁厂打交道，不必再使用喷灯和大锤，

sentences.en: and provide them with a quick way to kind of solve this problem.
sentences.zh: 为他们提供了一种快速解决问题的方法。

sentences.en: — And did you find in your reporting, Mike, that this was actually a more efficient way of getting rid of guns than, say, smashing them with a sledgehammer?
sentences.zh: ——迈克，你在报道中发现，这真的比用大锤砸碎枪支更有效率吗？

sentences.en: — So we visited the Gunbusters facility, which is located outside St. Louis.
sentences.zh: ——我们参观了位于圣路易斯郊外的“枪支终结者”工厂。

sentences.en: — Mind if I just record this, just so I can—
sentences.zh: ——介意我录一下吗，只是为了——

sentences.en: — And we got a tour of the place from the president of the company, Scott Reed, who was the son-in-law of the founder.
sentences.zh: ——我们由公司总裁斯科特·里德带领参观了工厂，他是创始人的女婿。

sentences.en: — So we are licensed by ATF, the same way any gun storm would be?
sentences.zh: ——所以我们是获得ATF许可的，和任何枪店一样？

sentences.en: — One of the striking things when we first go in there is they have rows and rows of walk-in
sentences.zh: ——当我们第一次进去时，最引人注目的是一排排的步入式保险库，

sentences.en: vaults filled with guns that they've been collecting from police agencies all over the country, which have to be destroyed.
sentences.zh: 里面装满了他们从全国各地警察机构收集来的、必须销毁的枪支。

sentences.en: — So you get a sense of the full scale of it.
sentences.zh: ——所以你能感受到它的规模之大。

sentences.en: You're talking thousands of weapons.
sentences.zh: 那是成千上万件武器。

sentences.en: — Wow.
— Can we, at any chance, take a look at how this rig works?
sentences.zh: ——我们有机会看看这台设备是怎么运作的吗？

sentences.en: — So this is our home run.
sentences.zh: ——这是我们的核心设备。

sentences.en: So there's two ways to look at it.
sentences.zh: 有两种看法。

sentences.en: It's either a scaled-up paper shredder, or it's a scaled-down car shredder.
sentences.zh: 它要么是一个大型碎纸机，要么是一个小型汽车粉碎机。

sentences.en: — And he showed us how the whole process works.
sentences.zh: ——他向我们展示了整个过程是如何运作的。

sentences.en: — And I have to say, it really is quite efficient.
sentences.zh: ——我不得不说，它确实非常高效。

sentences.en: — So it says now it's recording.
sentences.zh: ——现在显示正在录制。

sentences.en: Set it down.
sentences.zh: 放进去。

sentences.en: Drop it in.
sentences.zh: 丢进去。

sentences.en: — You can see from the camera inside the process as it happens.
sentences.zh: ——你可以从内部的摄像头看到整个过程。

sentences.en: The gun goes in one end, gets crunched up.
sentences.zh: 枪从一端进去，被压碎。

sentences.en: — So you see, you know, you get little pieces, and did it come through?
sentences.zh: ——你看，它变成了小碎片，出来了吗？

sentences.en: — And then comes out the other end as pieces.
sentences.zh: ——然后从另一端出来时就成了碎片。

sentences.en: And then there's a computer program that basically records the time and date, and the witness who was there, and all of that is sent to the police.
sentences.zh: 还有一个电脑程序会记录时间和日期，以及在场的见证人，所有这些都会发送给警方。

sentences.en: And the best thing about this process for law enforcement agencies is it's completely free.
sentences.zh: 对于执法机构来说，这个过程最好的地方在于它是完全免费的。

sentences.en: — It's free?
sentences.zh: ——免费的？

sentences.en: — It's free.
sentences.zh: ——免费的。

sentences.en: It costs them nothing.
sentences.zh: 他们不需要花一分钱。

sentences.en: And that is the big selling point and probably the main innovation of gunbusters.
sentences.zh: 这就是最大的卖点，也可能是“枪支终结者”的主要创新。

sentences.en: Now, there's a reason for how they can do that, and this is sort of the rub in the whole story, is that they dismantle the firearm before it's put through the machine.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们能做到这一点是有原因的，这也是整个故事的关键所在，那就是他们在把枪放入机器前会先拆解它。

sentences.en: And only one component is usually put through the pulverizer and crushed.
sentences.zh: 通常只有其中一个部件会被放入粉碎机中压碎。

sentences.en: All the rest of the parts of the gun are then sold online for anybody to purchase.
sentences.zh: 枪支的所有其他零件随后会在网上出售，任何人都可以购买。

sentences.en: — So you're telling me that this company that advertises itself as a pulverizer of guns is actually salvaging parts of them and then selling them off,
sentences.zh: ——所以你是说，这家自称是枪支粉碎机的公司，实际上是在回收枪支零件并转卖，

sentences.en: basically fueling a secondary market for guns.
sentences.zh: 基本上是在助推枪支的二级市场。

sentences.en: — That's exactly correct.
sentences.zh: ——完全正确。

sentences.en: And the way they do it has a lot to do with how guns are regulated in the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做的方式与美国对枪支的监管方式有很大关系。

sentences.en: — They dismantle each firearm that they collect from police agencies.
sentences.zh: ——他们拆解了从警察机构收集的每一支枪。

sentences.en: And in doing that, they remove the single piece of the gun that under the law and regulation is considered to be a firearm.
sentences.zh: 在拆解过程中，他们移除了法律和法规中被视为“枪支”的那唯一一个部件。

sentences.en: And that is called a receiver or the frame.
sentences.zh: 那个部件被称为机匣或枪身。

sentences.en: And what this component is, is really the central core of the gun to which all the other pieces are connected.
sentences.zh: 这个部件实际上是枪的核心，所有其他零件都连接在它上面。

sentences.en: So you've got the barrel, the stock, the trigger, slide, whatever, which all depend on having this one central piece in order to make it a working firearm.
sentences.zh: 所以你有枪管、枪托、扳机、套筒等等，所有这些都必须依赖这个核心部件才能成为一支能工作的枪。

sentences.en: Now, it gets a little complicated, but under the Gun Control Act of 1968, the receiver or the frame by itself is considered to be a firearm.
sentences.zh: 这有点复杂，但根据1968年的《枪支管制法》，机匣或枪身本身就被视为枪支。

sentences.en: So if you are gunbusters and you're telling the police that we're going to destroy the firearm, which is what they want,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是“枪支终结者”，你告诉警察我们要销毁这支枪（这正是他们想要的），

sentences.en: then you can get away with just simply destroying that one piece and say that you've destroyed the firearm.
sentences.zh: 那么你只需要销毁那一个部件，就可以说你已经销毁了这支枪。

sentences.en: This is not known by a lot of average people, but it is known to the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, and FirearMs.
sentences.zh: 普通人对此知之甚少，但酒精、烟草和火器管理局是知道的。

sentences.en: They don't have a problem with that.
sentences.zh: 他们对此没有意见。

sentences.en: They told us that, you know, the interpretation of the law is accurate.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我们，这种对法律的解读是准确的。

sentences.en: And that is an acceptable way of destroying a gun.
sentences.zh: 这是一种可以接受的销毁枪支的方式。

sentences.en: Now, once you destroy that one piece, you are left with a whole bunch of pieces that could be put back together again,
sentences.zh: 现在，一旦你销毁了那个部件，你就会剩下许多零件，它们本可以重新组装起来，

sentences.en: but they would still need that one missing piece in order to make a working gun.
sentences.zh: 但它们仍然需要那个缺失的部件才能成为一支能工作的枪。

sentences.en: And that is basically how gunbusters and other companies like it, there are a handful of others that do this, make their money.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是“枪支终结者”和其他类似公司（还有少数几家做这个的）赚钱的方式。

sentences.en: They take those pieces and they sell them as kits.
sentences.zh: 他们把这些零件拿走，作为套件出售。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Which means that you can buy one without having a background check.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你可以在没有背景调查的情况下买到一个。

sentences.en: You don't have to go through a licensed dealer to purchase one of these because it's not a functioning gun.
sentences.zh: 你不需要通过持牌经销商购买，因为它不是一支功能完整的枪。

sentences.en: But you can make it a functioning gun.
sentences.zh: 但你可以把它变成一支功能完整的枪。

sentences.en: You can then go and obtain a receiver or frame someplace else, put it together with one of these kits, and then you've got a reconstituted firearm.
sentences.zh: 你可以从别处弄到一个机匣或枪身，把它和这些套件组装在一起，你就得到了一支重组的枪支。

sentences.en: Now, if the client wants to pay for it, gunbusters will be happy to destroy the whole gun.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果客户愿意付费，“枪支终结者”也很乐意销毁整支枪。

sentences.en: But the police agency would have to give them money to do that.
sentences.zh: 但警察机构必须付钱给他们才行。

sentences.en: But is that what is actually happening?
sentences.zh: 但实际情况真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: That these parts are, in fact, being repurposed into new guns?
sentences.zh: 这些零件实际上被重新利用，变成了新的枪支？

sentences.en: It's a little bit difficult to know exactly how often that happens and what the parts kits are used for.
sentences.zh: 很难确切知道这种情况发生的频率，以及这些零件包的用途。

sentences.en: Certainly there are people who are gun collectors or enthusiasts who might be looking for a piece,
sentences.zh: 当然，有一些枪支收藏家或爱好者可能正在寻找某个部件，

sentences.en: especially of an old gun that's no longer available and they want to be able to maintain or fix a firearm.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那些已经停产的老枪，他们希望能借此维护或修理枪支。

sentences.en: But that wouldn't account for the frequency with which these kits are sold.
sentences.zh: 但这无法解释这些零件包销售的频率。

sentences.en: And if you go, for instance, on the website called Gun Broker, which is the world's largest online site for buying and selling firearms,
sentences.zh: 如果你去看看像 Gun Broker 这样的网站，它是全球最大的枪支买卖在线平台，

sentences.en: that is where most of Gun Buster's kits are sold.
sentences.zh: 那正是 Gun Buster 大部分零件包的销售渠道。

sentences.en: You will find other sellers saying in their listing, oh, you can pair this with a kit from Gun Buster's and make a complete working gun.
sentences.zh: 你会发现其他卖家在商品描述中说，哦，你可以把这个和 Gun Buster 的零件包配在一起，组装成一把完整的可用枪支。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So we know that people certainly are buying these kits with that in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，人们购买这些零件包时确实是抱着这种想法的。

sentences.en: And we know that most of the guns that Gun Buster's takes in from police agencies do wind up being sold in this way.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道，Gun Buster 从警察局接收的大部分枪支，最终确实都是以这种方式被卖掉的。

sentences.en: So there's no reason to believe that a large portion of these kits are being purchased for the exact purpose of being able to put them back together again and make a working gun.
sentences.zh: 因此，没有理由不相信，很大一部分零件包被购买，正是为了能把它们重新组装成一把可用的枪。

sentences.en: But it sounds like we don't have any way of knowing exactly what happens to any given kit, to any given set of gun parts.
sentences.zh: 但听起来我们似乎无法确切知道任何特定的零件包，或者任何一套枪支零件最终去了哪里。

sentences.en: Part of the problem with trying to figure out what exactly happens to these gun kits that are sold online by Gun Busters is they don't include the serial number
sentences.zh: 试图弄清楚 Gun Busters 在网上销售的这些枪支零件包最终流向何处，部分困难在于它们不包含序列号，

sentences.en: because that one component of the gun that they actually did destroy is the one component that has the serial number.
sentences.zh: 因为他们唯一真正销毁的那个枪支组件，恰恰就是带有序列号的那个组件。

sentences.en: So the remaining parts most of the time do not have any kind of a way of tracing them.
sentences.zh: 所以剩下的零件大多数时候没有任何追踪方式。

sentences.en: And one of the concerns from gun violence groups is that there are people out there who are capable of making their own receivers and frames, which are not serialized.
sentences.zh: 枪支暴力预防组织担心的其中一点是，有些人有能力制造自己的机匣和枪身，而这些部件是没有序列号的。

sentences.en: These are commonly referred to as ghost guns because they are not traceable.
sentences.zh: 这些通常被称为“幽灵枪”，因为它们无法被追踪。

sentences.en: And you would have a working gun with no way of knowing where any of the components came from.
sentences.zh: 你最终会得到一把可用的枪，却完全无法知道它的任何组件来自哪里。

sentences.en: Okay, so all of this is pretty shocking.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这一切真是令人震惊。

sentences.en: I mean, I assume the people who wanted a gun eliminated because they felt like it posed a specific threat would be pretty surprised that that gun was just repurposed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想那些希望销毁枪支的人，是因为他们觉得枪支构成了特定的威胁，如果他们知道那把枪只是被重新利用了，一定会非常惊讶。

sentences.en: It feels like a bait-and-switch and also potentially a total boon for this company.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是一种诱导式欺诈，而且对这家公司来说可能是一笔巨大的横财。

sentences.en: Well, it certainly has been a boon for the company and others like it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这对该公司及其他类似公司来说确实是一笔横财。

sentences.en: Gun Busters says that they've taken in more than 200,000 firearms over the past decade from about 950 police agencies across the country.
sentences.zh: Gun Busters 表示，在过去十年里，他们从全国约 950 个警察局接收了超过 20 万支枪支。

sentences.en: Their biggest client being the Michigan State Police.
sentences.zh: 他们最大的客户是密歇根州警察局。

sentences.en: So when you figure the amount of money they've been making in selling these parts kits, they've made millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 所以当你计算他们通过销售这些零件包赚取的金额时，他们已经赚了数百万美元。

sentences.en: So it's certainly been lucrative for these businesses.
sentences.zh: 所以这对这些企业来说确实是利润丰厚的。

sentences.en: When you take into account the total number of guns in America, it may not seem like a big number we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 当你考虑到美国枪支的总数时，我们谈论的这个数字似乎并不大。

sentences.en: But, you know, if you consider the havoc that one firearm is capable of wreaking, or if someone simply wants to make sure a gun is taken out of circulation,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果你考虑到一把枪可能造成的破坏，或者如果有人只是想确保一把枪退出流通，

sentences.en: you know, they may now be surprised by this to find out that they feel like they've been led astray and not knowing what was actually happening to these guns.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们现在可能会因为发现自己被误导，且不知道这些枪支的真实去向而感到惊讶。

sentences.en: But the reality is actually a lot more complicated.
sentences.zh: 但现实情况其实要复杂得多。

sentences.en: And if you take a closer look at how this came to be, in many ways it was totally predictable.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细观察这一切是如何发生的，在很多方面，这完全是可以预见的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是 Benjamin Poulin。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是 Mark Ronson。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档关于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜店用黑胶唱片做 DJ 的那个年代，每天晚上你都要带着 300 件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你会把 DJ 台变成一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，陈列着精美的 50 年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是 Winnalou。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢尝试捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是 Sam Azersky，我每天负责创作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人们制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Mike, before the break, you explained to us that Gunbusters, a private company, is taking unwanted guns across the country and is generally understood to be destroying them,
sentences.zh: Mike，休息前你向我们解释说，Gunbusters 是一家私人公司，它从全国各地接收不需要的枪支，人们普遍认为他们会销毁这些枪支，

sentences.en: but is actually only destroying part of that gun and selling the rest for profit.
sentences.zh: 但实际上他们只销毁了枪支的一部分，然后把剩下的部分卖掉获利。

sentences.en: But you also said that, while surprising, it's also totally predictable.
sentences.zh: 但你也说过，虽然令人惊讶，但这完全是可以预见的。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下这一点。

sentences.en: When you look at the actual agreements that Gunbusters entered into with law enforcement agencies,
sentences.zh: 当你查看 Gunbusters 与执法机构签订的实际协议时，

sentences.en: they make pretty clear in the text of these contracts that Gunbusters intends to do exactly what it does.
sentences.zh: 他们在合同文本中非常明确地表明，Gunbusters 打算做的正是他们现在所做的。

sentences.en: I'll give you an example.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个例子。

sentences.en: The sheriff's office in Denton County, Texas, has an agreement in which it says that no money will be exchanged
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州丹顿县治安官办公室有一份协议，其中规定不会有任何金钱往来，

sentences.en: or reimbursed as a result of the destruction of the firearms, meaning that the sheriff's office doesn't have to pay anybody.
sentences.zh: 也不会因为销毁枪支而进行报销，这意味着治安官办公室不需要支付任何人费用。

sentences.en: But then farther down, it also says that Gunbusters will sell salvaged parts and scrap metal.
sentences.zh: 但随后在合同后面，它也写明 Gunbusters 将出售回收的零件和废金属。

sentences.en: Now, scrap metal is understandable because when you put the gun through the pulverizer, what comes out the other end are just shredded pieces of metal,
sentences.zh: 废金属是可以理解的，因为当你把枪放进粉碎机时，出来的是粉碎后的金属片，

sentences.en: and they do make a little bit of money by selling that.
sentences.zh: 他们通过出售这些确实能赚一点钱。

sentences.en: But salvaged parts is something completely different, and that refers to the gun kits.
sentences.zh: 但回收零件是完全不同的概念，指的就是那些枪支零件包。

sentences.en: That is really where the most of the money comes from.
sentences.zh: 那才是他们大部分收入的来源。

sentences.en: So this is not a huge mystery to the police departments that are entering into these agreements with Gunbusters.
sentences.zh: 所以对于与 Gunbusters 签订这些协议的警察局来说，这并不是什么巨大的谜团。

sentences.en: So the city officials and police departments contracting with Gunbusters do know that the guns aren't actually being destroyed.
sentences.zh: 所以与 Gunbusters 签约的城市官员和警察局确实知道这些枪支并没有被真正销毁。

sentences.en: I mean, are they reading the contract and fully aware that this is the deal?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们是在阅读合同并完全意识到这就是交易内容吗？

sentences.en: Well, so that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: From my review of a lot of city council, town council, local board authorizations of these contracts,
sentences.zh: 根据我对许多市议会、镇议会和地方委员会批准这些合同的审查，

sentences.en: what you often see is what you might expect is that they're sometimes approving a whole slate of contracts all at once.
sentences.zh: 你经常会看到你可能预料到的情况，即他们有时会一次性批准一整批合同。

sentences.en: It's often done on a very quick up-and-down vote.
sentences.zh: 这通常是在非常快速的投票中完成的。

sentences.en: There's no reading of the contract.
sentences.zh: 根本没有人阅读合同。

sentences.en: There's no questions asked.
sentences.zh: 也没有人提出任何问题。

sentences.en: So the police and the sheriff's offices, they know what's in these contracts.
sentences.zh: 所以警察局和治安官办公室，他们知道合同里写了什么。

sentences.en: But they also know that if they were to pay for this, it would require going to the local elected officials and asking for money.
sentences.zh: 但他们也知道，如果他们要为此付费，就需要去找当地民选官员申请资金。

sentences.en: It would mean asking for a line item in their budget.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要在预算中申请一个单独的项目。

sentences.en: And that's not something that most of these police departments want to do or have to get involved in.
sentences.zh: 而这并不是大多数警察局想要做或想要参与的事情。

sentences.en: And the elected officials often have just no idea what's in these contracts.
sentences.zh: 而民选官员通常根本不知道合同里写了什么。

sentences.en: All they know is that they've entered into some sort of an agreement to destroy the guns.
sentences.zh: 他们只知道他们签署了某种销毁枪支的协议。

sentences.en: Because that's how it's described.
sentences.zh: 因为描述就是这么说的。

sentences.en: The guns are going to be destroyed.
sentences.zh: 枪支将被销毁。

sentences.en: And to a layperson, that's not a very complicated thought.
sentences.zh: 对于外行来说，这并不是一个复杂的想法。

sentences.en: But the details are where the devil is.
sentences.zh: 但魔鬼往往藏在细节里。

sentences.en: And most of the elected officials that I came across have no idea that's actually what's happening.
sentences.zh: 而我接触过的大多数民选官员都不知道实际发生的情况。

sentences.en: Okay, then, gunbusters isn't lying to anybody.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么 Gunbusters 并没有对任何人撒谎。

sentences.en: They technically, in the contract, are saying exactly what they're offering.
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，他们在合同中明确说明了他们提供的内容。

sentences.en: And police departments and other groups contracting with them are maybe just willfully ignoring the fine print for the reasons you just described.
sentences.zh: 而与他们签约的警察局和其他团体，可能只是因为你刚才描述的原因，故意忽略了细则。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, the entire point of these programs is destroying guns.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，这些项目的全部意义在于销毁枪支。

sentences.en: How does this meet that goal in any way?
sentences.zh: 这在任何方面是如何实现这一目标的呢？

sentences.en: So this is where the law and regulations around firearms becomes important.
sentences.zh: 这就是关于枪支的法律和法规变得重要的地方。

sentences.en: Because if you remember, I mentioned the Gun Control Act, which was a law passed in 1968 where they defined firearms in that particular way.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你还记得的话，我提到了《枪支管制法》，这是一项 1968 年通过的法律，他们在其中以特定的方式定义了枪支。

sentences.en: When that law was passed and the regulations were drafted to enact it, it was not the intention at the time to create this sort of loophole that's now being exploited, if you will.
sentences.zh: 当该法律通过并起草相关法规来实施时，当时的意图并不是要制造这种现在被利用的漏洞。

sentences.en: Well, the intention in delineating what a receiver or a frame was was to actually to make the regulations a little bit tighter.
sentences.zh: 嗯，界定什么是机匣或枪身的意图，实际上是为了让法规稍微严格一点。

sentences.en: It was not meant to create that loophole at all.
sentences.zh: 根本不是为了制造那个漏洞。

sentences.en: Mike, it sounds like in this kind of twisted way, this law that was supposed to be restrictive is now actually perversely making it harder to get rid of guns.
sentences.zh: Mike，听起来以这种扭曲的方式，这项本应具有限制性的法律，现在反而以一种反常的方式让处理枪支变得更加困难了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: I think that the intent of the regulations that were created after the 1968 Act never foresaw the situation where it would somehow allow for guns that were intended to be destroyed
sentences.zh: 我认为 1968 年法案之后制定的法规，其初衷从未预见到会出现这种情况，即它会以某种方式允许那些本应被销毁的枪支，

sentences.en: to instead be essentially recycled in some fashion back out into the civilian market.
sentences.zh: 反而以某种方式被重新循环回民用市场。

sentences.en: And yet in this one way, it has had the opposite effect.
sentences.zh: 然而在这一方面，它却产生了相反的效果。

sentences.en: But it seems like the obvious solution here would be to change the legal definition of a gun.
sentences.zh: 但看起来这里显而易见的解决方案是改变枪支的法律定义。

sentences.en: I mean, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对吧？

sentences.en: Or at least for these governments to just pay the fee to destroy the entire gun, which you said earlier, gunbusters would do.
sentences.zh: 或者至少让这些政府支付费用来销毁整把枪，你之前说过 Gunbusters 会这样做。

sentences.en: Well, certainly if the police agencies and the towns that support them would be willing to pay to have gunbusters destroy the complete firearm, that would be the simplest solution.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，如果警察机构和支持它们的小镇愿意付费让 Gunbusters 销毁完整的枪支，那将是最简单的解决方案。

sentences.en: But Scott Reed, when I visited gunbusters, told me that some 98 percent of their clients opt not to do that.
sentences.zh: 但 Scott Reed 在我访问 Gunbusters 时告诉我，大约 98% 的客户选择不这样做。

sentences.en: But the other option would be to try to somehow change the regulations around what defines a receiver or a frame.
sentences.zh: 但另一个选择是尝试以某种方式改变关于什么是机匣或枪身的法规。

sentences.en: And that seems very unlikely.
sentences.zh: 但这看起来不太可能。

sentences.en: I mean, first of all, you would have to either change the law or the ATF interpretation of the law and the regulations.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，首先，你必须要么修改法律，要么修改 ATF 对法律和法规的解释。

sentences.en: And neither of those things seem likely to happen in the current climate.
sentences.zh: 而在当前环境下，这两者似乎都不太可能发生。

sentences.en: So even though this is clearly a loophole that was not meant to cause the effect that it is having,
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管这显然是一个本不该造成目前这种后果的漏洞，

sentences.en: now that it exists, it's hard to roll back, especially in the context of the super political nature of everything related to guns.
sentences.zh: 但既然它已经存在，就很难撤销，特别是在所有与枪支相关的事物都高度政治化的背景下。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it was a given at one time that police departments that wanted to get rid of guns could easily do so.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，曾经有一段时间，想要处理掉枪支的警察局可以很容易地做到这一点。

sentences.en: And now you've got situations in which there are actually some states where mostly Republican legislatures are passing laws that actually prevent police departments from destroying guns in their inventory.
sentences.zh: 而现在你面临的情况是，实际上在一些州，主要是共和党控制的立法机构正在通过法律，阻止警察局销毁其库存中的枪支。

sentences.en: And so instead, what they're forced to do is to auction them off or sell them.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们被迫采取的做法是拍卖或出售它们。

sentences.en: So this is where you see this great divide happening, where you've got mostly red states and communities that are making it more difficult for police to get rid of guns.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是你看到这种巨大分歧的地方，在大多数红色州和社区，他们让警察处理枪支变得更加困难。

sentences.en: And you've got mostly blue cities and states where the opposite is happening.
sentences.zh: 而在大多数蓝色城市和州，情况则恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Mike, I'm curious how Scott Reed, the man who runs Gunbusters, how do you think he feels about all of this?
sentences.zh: Mike，我很好奇经营 Gunbusters 的 Scott Reed，你认为他对此有何感想？

sentences.en: I mean, he must know that some people are under the impression that he really is taking guns out of circulation when we know he's not.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他一定知道有些人认为他真的在让枪支退出流通，而我们知道他并没有这样做。

sentences.en: I talked to him about this a couple of times.
sentences.zh: 我和他谈过几次这个问题。

sentences.en: Do you guys have like a philosophy around this?
sentences.zh: 你们对此有什么理念吗？

sentences.en: I mean, what is your...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你们的……

sentences.en: And he acknowledges that there are people that he deals with who do want the full gun to be destroyed.
sentences.zh: 他承认，他接触的人中确实有人希望整把枪被销毁。

sentences.en: And from his point of view, if they're willing to pay to do that, then he will do that.
sentences.zh: 从他的角度来看，如果他们愿意为此付费，那么他就会这样做。

sentences.en: I think at some point, you know, both sides see things in us that, you know, we can take as a positive and both sides see things that can take as a negative.
sentences.zh: 我想在某种程度上，你知道，双方都在我们身上看到了他们可以认为是积极的东西，也看到了他们可以认为是消极的东西。

sentences.en: I don't know that we're actively convincing anyone, hey, you should destroy your guns, you know, these...
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们是否在积极说服任何人，嘿，你应该销毁你的枪，你知道，这些……

sentences.en: At the end of the day, though, he's a businessman.
sentences.zh: 不过归根结底，他是个商人。

sentences.en: He's in the business of making money and providing a service to law enforcement agencies.
sentences.zh: 他的生意就是赚钱并为执法机构提供服务。

sentences.en: So, you know, I think we walk that tightrope of how are we, you know, a public service where we're helping apartments.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为我们在走钢丝，我们如何成为一种公共服务，我们如何帮助部门。

sentences.en: We are taking guns out, you know, of the system.
sentences.zh: 我们确实在把枪从系统中拿出来，你知道。

sentences.en: But then, you know, parts are still, you know, remain out there, so.
sentences.zh: 但后来，你知道，零件仍然，你知道，留在外面，所以。

sentences.en: He can say that even the method that they do follow of taking the gun apart and selling the pieces, you know,
sentences.zh: 他可以说，即使他们遵循的拆解枪支并出售零件的方法，你知道，

sentences.en: it is succeeding in taking guns out of the community in which the police department had them.
sentences.zh: 它确实成功地将枪支从警察局所在的社区中移除了。

sentences.en: And so, you know, if a police agency somewhere has a bunch of guns from a buyback and they want to get them out of the community and off the street,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果某个地方的警察机构从回购计划中获得了一堆枪支，并且他们想把它们从社区和街道上清理出去，

sentences.en: giving them the gunbusters at least does that.
sentences.zh: 把它们交给 Gunbusters 至少能做到这一点。

sentences.en: But, you know, of course, if they don't pay to have the thing completely destroyed, then the parts of those guns will find their way back out somewhere.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，当然，如果他们不付费让枪支被彻底销毁，那么这些枪支的零件就会流向其他地方。

sentences.en: It just may not be in that particular community.
sentences.zh: 只是可能不在那个特定的社区而已。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: On the one hand, you could see gunbusters as exploiting the vagaries in the law and the desire to get guns off the street to make money.
sentences.zh: 一方面，你可以认为 Gunbusters 是在利用法律的模糊性和人们希望将枪支从街头清理出去的愿望来赚钱。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, gunbusters is being pretty straightforward in what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，Gunbusters 在他们所做的事情上表现得相当直率。

sentences.en: They see a market and they're not being untruthful about the service they're providing.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了市场，并且对于他们提供的服务并没有不诚实。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe people should just read the fine print.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许人们应该仔细阅读细则。

sentences.en: So, how do you think about this, Mike?
sentences.zh: 那么，Mike，你是怎么看待这件事的？

sentences.en: It really struck me going into this that as easy as it is to obtain a gun in America these days, it's surprisingly difficult to get rid of one.
sentences.zh: 在深入了解这件事后，我真正感到震惊的是，如今在美国获得一把枪是多么容易，而想要处理掉一把枪却出奇地困难。

sentences.en: And the fact that we're engaged in this semantic debate about what isn't a firearm and what's not a firearm, it just goes to how polarized everything is on this whole subject.
sentences.zh: 而且我们陷入了关于什么是枪支、什么不是枪支的语义辩论，这恰恰说明了在这个问题上一切是多么的两极分化。

sentences.en: And so, the real reason why it's so difficult to destroy a gun has little to do with the means in which you would physically do it.
sentences.zh: 所以，销毁枪支之所以如此困难，其真正原因与你物理上销毁它的手段关系不大。

sentences.en: It has more to do with what it means to have a firearm and the ability to regulate them is really what it boils down to.
sentences.zh: 它更多地与拥有枪支意味着什么有关，而监管它们的能力才是问题的核心所在。

sentences.en: And even when there are genuine efforts to destroy guns, it doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 即使有真正的努力去销毁枪支，也无法实现。

sentences.en: I mean, there are enough forces against it, there's enough of a market there that it fails.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有足够多的力量在反对它，那里有足够的市场，以至于它失败了。

sentences.en: That is one of the great ironies, is that at the end of the day, even the best intentions when it comes to how to destroy a gun are often thwarted.
sentences.zh: 这就是最大的讽刺之一，归根结底，即使在如何销毁枪支的问题上，最好的意图也往往会受挫。

sentences.en: And the people who think they're doing some service to their community by taking guns off the street, they are led to believe,
sentences.zh: 而那些认为自己通过将枪支从街头清理出去是在为社区服务的人，他们被引导去相信，

sentences.en: often by their elected leaders who aren't paying attention, that this in fact is what's happening.
sentences.zh: 通常是由他们选出的领导人，因为他们没有关注到，事实上这就是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And it turns out that it's not.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明并非如此。

sentences.en: Mike, thank you.
sentences.zh: 迈克，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Following the Times investigation, Michigan State Police, which sends gunbusters about 11,000 guns a year and is its largest client,
sentences.zh: 在《泰晤士报》调查之后，密歇根州警方——他们每年向Gunbusters公司发送约11000支枪支，是其最大的客户——

sentences.en: has temporarily paused its contract with the company.
sentences.zh: 已经暂时中止了与该公司的合同。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Hezbollah, the Iran-backed militant group, said on Monday that one of its commanders had been killed in a strike in southern Lebanon near the country's border with Israel.
sentences.zh: 伊朗支持的激进组织真主党周一表示，其一名指挥官在黎巴嫩南部靠近该国与以色列边境的一次袭击中丧生。

sentences.en: Israel and Hezbollah have treated increasingly intense cross-border fire since Israel's war against Hamas in Gaza began three months ago.
sentences.zh: 自三个月前以色列在加沙对哈马斯发动战争以来，以色列和真主党之间的跨境交火日益激烈。

sentences.en: The latest attack, which follows an Israeli strike last week that killed senior Hamas leaders in Lebanon,
sentences.zh: 这次最新的袭击，紧随上周以色列在黎巴嫩打死哈马斯高级领导人的空袭之后，

sentences.en: has added to fears that the war in Gaza could erupt into a wider regional conflict.
sentences.zh: 加剧了人们对加沙战争可能演变成更大规模地区冲突的担忧。

sentences.en: And in an interview with the Times,
sentences.zh: 而在接受《泰晤士报》采访时，

sentences.en: the chief spokesman for the Israeli military said that Israel is expected to begin to shift away from a large-scale ground and air campaign in Gaza to a more targeted phase in its war against Hamas,
sentences.zh: 以色列军方首席发言人表示，预计以色列将开始从加沙的大规模地面和空中行动，转向针对哈马斯战争的更具针对性的阶段，

sentences.en: involving fewer troops and airstrikes.
sentences.zh: 涉及更少的部队和空袭。

sentences.en: The disclosure comes as U.S.
sentences.zh: 这一披露正值美国

sentences.en: Secretary of State Antony Blinken visits leaders in the Middle East this week on a trip aimed at preventing the fighting from expanding.
sentences.zh: 国务卿安东尼·布林肯本周访问中东领导人，此行旨在防止战事扩大。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否喝到断片才能睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
